title: Quantization-freed capacity: from-scratch depthwise-separable trunk + unified single-head field, weights trained for int8 export
hypothesis: 20+ rounds since champion (exp-35, 743.07 m) have swept nearly every decode/output family (VQ codebook, GMM, dense per-patch consensus, spatial MoE, retrieve-rerank, factorized axes, coarse-to-fine, coordinate-generated field) and nearly every trunk-objective family (contrastive, reconstruction/canonicalization translators, ShuffleNetV2-pretrained, five from-scratch variants) on top of or in place of champion's field+soft-argmax decode, and all of them lost. The single closest post-champion result in the whole history is exp-42 (846.42 m, contrastive-pretrained from-scratch trunk) -- the ONE experiment that changed only the trunk's training objective while leaving the champion's full-capacity field/decode/C4-ensemble shape completely untouched. Every from-scratch trunk ever tried (exp 41-55) was a small plain conv stack (~130k params) next to champion's 190k-param pretrained trunk feeding a ~570k-param single field head; every experiment that also SPLIT capacity across two or more heads (the exp-12 gate kept in several designs, and explicitly the three independent dispatcher/specialist attempts exp-30/46/59) lost, exp-59 catastrophically (2134 m) despite a coherent gradient-interference hypothesis -- its own pre-registered risk note said capacity-per-regime could dominate over gradient interference, and the result supports exactly that: capacity, not decode shape or gradient crosstalk, is what this design has been starved of every time a from-scratch trunk or a split-capacity design has been tried. This round bans the champion's exact pretrained trunk outright, which finally forces the one lever no prior round has pulled: instead of accepting whatever capacity a from-scratch trunk happens to have at float32 byte cost, train every trunk/field/confidence weight tensor to tolerate int8 rounding (a fixed, non-learned round-to-grid transform with a straight-through gradient, applied every forward pass) and export the deployed artifact through real int8 weight quantization (onnxruntime dynamic quantization, not a training-time simulation left un-exported) -- turning the 4-byte-per-weight cost that has capped every from-scratch trunk's width so far into a 1-byte-per-weight cost, and spending the freed budget on both a wider trunk AND a single larger unified field (deleting the exp-12 gate/dark-expert split entirely, since the evidence above says specialization has been costing capacity, not buying it).
method: In model/model.py: delete the mobilenet_v3_small import, _build_pretrained_trunk, PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH, and the ImageNet mean/std buffers entirely -- no torchvision import anywhere in the file. Replace with a from-scratch, never-pretrained depthwise-separable conv trunk (a stem 3->64 regular 3x3 conv stride 2, then three depthwise-separable stride-2 blocks 64->128->224->320, BatchNorm2d+ReLU6 after every conv, 128x128 input -> 8x8x320 output -- 4x wider than every from-scratch trunk tried in exps 41-55 because depthwise-separable convs buy width per byte far more cheaply than the plain conv stacks those experiments used). Delete self.dark_logits and self.gate entirely (the exp-12 two-expert blend) -- one unified loc_logits Linear head reads the new trunk's [320-d GAP + 8-channel/64-cell layout-squeeze code] descriptor, same layout-squeeze mechanism as today just re-widthed. Raise GRID_K from 32 to 40 (1024 -> 1600 cells, ~175 m cells instead of ~220 m) since the freed byte budget affords a finer field; DECODE_BETA, the Gaussian-smoothed-CE target, and the sharpened-soft-argmax decode formula are otherwise byte-identical, just operating over the new grid size. The C4 rotation-vote (4x forward pass, average field logits over the crop's 90-degree rotations) is kept -- it is a previously-validated, causally distinct mechanism (exp 16, +33%) this experiment is not testing -- but its code necessarily changes because there is no longer a gated blend to average before the vote: logits4 = self.loc_logits(...) directly, then the same reshape(4,n,-1).mean(dim=0). Confidence head is rebuilt with re-dimensioned Linear layers reading the new (320-d GAP + peak + entropy + sharp/unsharp gap) descriptor -- same three shape-derived features as today, same detached-gradient contract, just resized for the new GAP width. Add a QATConv2d/QATLinear module pair (thin nn.Conv2d/nn.Linear subclasses) that fake-quantize self.weight every forward call via a symmetric per-tensor 8-bit round-to-grid straight-through estimator (scale = weight.detach().abs().max()/127, quantized = round(weight/scale).clamp(-127,127)*scale, gradient passes straight through the round) before calling the normal functional conv/linear op -- used for every weighted layer in the trunk, layout_squeeze, loc_logits, and conf_head (NOT the tiny confidence-head bias-only ops or the fixed grid-center buffers). In model/train.py: replace the two-LR-group optimizer (trunk_params at 1e-4, head_params at 1e-3 -- a fine-tuning schedule that only makes sense for a pretrained trunk) with a single param group at 1e-3 for the whole from-scratch model, since there are no pretrained features to protect from early large gradients; update the `info["init"]` string to reflect from-scratch init with weight fake-quantization. After the existing epoch loop, calibration, and float32 export_onnx call (kept as an intermediate sanity artifact), add one final step: onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic(model_input=<float32 onnx path>, model_output=<same models/<area>.onnx path>, weight_type=QuantType.QInt8) with default (per-tensor, no reduce_range) settings, overwriting the scored artifact with the real int8-weight ONNX -- input/output tensor names, shapes, and the float32-in/float32-out contract are unchanged by dynamic quantization (only Conv/Gemm/MatMul weight tensors become int8; activations stay float32 end to end), so pipeline/score.py needs no changes. Confusability-weighted sampling (exp 35), TRAIN_REALIZATIONS, EPOCH_MULT, per-epoch resampling, and the calibration procedure are all left exactly as today -- this experiment's ONE hypothesis is capacity, not data strategy, and mixing in a sampler change would confound attribution.
expected_outcome: If capacity -- not decode/output family, not gradient interference between lighting regimes -- has been the real remaining ceiling since exp-35, this should beat exp-42's 846.42 m (the best post-champion result, achieved by a trunk-objective swap alone at champion's original capacity) by a clear margin, plausibly landing in the 600-850 m range and possibly at or below champion's 743.07 m if the freed budget genuinely buys back more accuracy than int8 rounding costs. Falsification forks: (a) if the metric lands clearly better than 846 m with a real ONNX byte size comfortably under the 4 MiB gate (confirming the freed-capacity mechanism actually fired, not just a lucky init), the capacity hypothesis is supported and future rounds should keep exploring this axis -- wider trunk still, finer grid still, or a second int8 quantization pass with per-channel weights for less rounding loss; (b) if the metric is flat or worse than 846 m despite a healthy training loss curve and a comfortably-sized ONNX, int8 rounding noise (not float32 byte cost) is the real tax on a from-scratch trunk, and future rounds should try a coarser quantization (e.g. 6 bits reserved for the most sensitive layers) or abandon the quantization-capacity axis and treat champion's decode/field shape as near-optimal, redirecting to calibration/coverage as CLAUDE.md SS6's remaining secondary levers; (c) if the exported ONNX is NOT meaningfully smaller than a float32 equivalent (dynamic quantization silently failed to touch the weighted ops, e.g. due to an opset mismatch), this is an implementation failure to diagnose and retry, not evidence against the hypothesis -- the byte size gate result should be checked first before reading the accuracy number as informative.
eli5: Every recent attempt to swap out the one part of the model we're now required to remove made things worse, and the pattern points at a simple reason: the replacement parts were always smaller and cheaper than the piece they replaced, because the model has to fit in a fixed 4-megabyte file. This experiment tries a trick borrowed from how phones shrink apps: train the model's numbers to already sit on a coarse, round grid (like rounding every price to the nearest dollar instead of the nearest cent), so that when we later squeeze those numbers down to take a quarter of the storage space each, almost nothing is lost. That squeeze buys back enough room to build a genuinely bigger, single-focus model instead of the small or split-up replacements that kept losing.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128x128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: a brand-new, never-pretrained conv stack built from cheap 'depthwise-separable' layers (a mobile-phone-style trick that gets more width per byte than a plain conv stack) -- 4x wider than every from-scratch attempt tried before, since the freed storage budget (see Training signal below) makes the extra width affordable

stages.name: Rotation fan
stages.detail: the crop and its four 90-degree turns still all travel through the same network side by side and their summaries are averaged, but there is no longer a bright/dark blend step before that averaging -- one unified head all the way through

stages.name: Location field
stages.detail: the old two-expert bright/dark blend is deleted -- a single, bigger scorer reads the new wider descriptor and produces one map-cell heat map, at a finer 40x40 grid instead of 32x32 since the freed byte budget affords sharper cells

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: same mechanism as before -- sharpen the heat map's contrast, then answer with its balance point -- now computed over the finer 1,600-cell grid

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: recomputed from the new wider descriptor's shape (same recipe: crisp hotspot = sure, smear = unsure) since the old two-expert-derived inputs it used to read no longer exist

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: every weight in the new trunk and field is nudged, on every training step, to already sit close to a coarse 256-level rounding grid (a fixed, non-learned round-to-grid step with a pass-through gradient) -- so the model learns to be good WHILE living on that grid, instead of being trained freely and then rounded as an afterthought

stages.name: Deployment export
stages.detail: after training, the model's weights are actually converted to that coarse grid and stored at one-quarter the file size (real 8-bit storage, not just a training-time simulation), and it is this smaller file -- not a full-size one -- that gets scored and would fly

implementation_brief:
FILES: model/model.py and model/train.py only; pipeline/score.py's contract (1x3x128x128 float32 [0,1] input named 'frame', [[u,v,conf]] float32 output named 'uvc', opset 17, dynamo=False) is UNCHANGED and must keep passing unmodified.

model/model.py:
1) Delete: `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, `_build_pretrained_trunk`, `PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH`, `IMAGENET_MEAN`, `IMAGENET_STD`, the `norm_mean`/`norm_std` buffers, `self.dark_logits`, `self.gate`. No torchvision import may remain anywhere in the file. No `.pt`/`.pth`/`.bin`/`.safetensors` file is loaded anywhere -- this trunk is 100% randomly initialized.
2) Add two thin subclasses near the top of the file: `class QATConv2d(nn.Conv2d)` and `class QATLinear(nn.Linear)`, each overriding `forward(self, x)` to compute `w = self.weight; scale = (w.detach().abs().max() / 127.0).clamp_min(1e-8); wq = w + (torch.clamp(torch.round(w / scale), -127, 127) * scale - w).detach()` (the `+ (... ).detach()` idiom is the straight-through estimator: forward value is the rounded/rescaled weight, backward gradient flows to `w` unchanged) and then calls `F.conv2d`/`F.linear` with `wq` and `self.bias` (plus the Conv2d's stride/padding/groups/dilation passed through). Import `torch.nn.functional as F`.
3) Replace `_build_pretrained_trunk` with a `_build_trunk()` that returns an `nn.Sequential` (or small custom `nn.Module`) built ONLY from `QATConv2d`, `nn.BatchNorm2d`, `nn.ReLU6`, in this shape: stem `QATConv2d(3, 64, 3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False)` -> BN(64) -> ReLU6 [128->64]; block1 depthwise `QATConv2d(64, 64, 3, stride=2, padding=1, groups=64, bias=False)` -> BN(64) -> ReLU6 -> pointwise `QATConv2d(64, 128, 1, bias=False)` -> BN(128) -> ReLU6 [64->32]; block2 depthwise `QATConv2d(128,128,3,stride=2,padding=1,groups=128,bias=False)` -> BN -> ReLU6 -> pointwise `QATConv2d(128,224,1,bias=False)` -> BN(224) -> ReLU6 [32->16]; block3 depthwise `QATConv2d(224,224,3,stride=2,padding=1,groups=224,bias=False)` -> BN -> ReLU6 -> pointwise `QATConv2d(224,320,1,bias=False)` -> BN(320) -> ReLU6 [16->8]. Output: 320 channels at 8x8.
4) `GRID_K = 40` (was 32).
5) In `TinyLocNet.__init__`: `self.features = _build_trunk()`; probe with a zero tensor to get `feat_ch=320, fmap_hw=8` exactly as today; `self.layout_squeeze = nn.Conv2d(feat_ch, layout_ch, 1)` -> keep as plain `nn.Conv2d` (small, not worth fake-quantizing, avoids QAT-wrapping every last layer); `self.loc_logits = QATLinear(feat_ch + layout_ch*fmap_hw*fmap_hw, grid_k*grid_k)`; delete `self.dark_logits`, `self.gate`; `self.conf_head = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(feat_ch+3, 48), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(48,1))` (plain Linear -- confidence head stays unquantized, it's tiny and not exported through the same accuracy-critical path). Keep `self.conf_shift` buffer and `cell_u`/`cell_v` exactly as today (grid_k now 40).
6) In `forward`: remove `lum`, `g4`, `bright_logits4`, `dark_logits4` entirely (no gate, no brightness feature needed since there's no blend to condition). `x4 = _c4_stack(x)` unchanged. `fmap = self.features(x4)` -- NOTE: no ImageNet normalization anymore, feed raw [0,1] pixels directly (the from-scratch trunk has no reason to expect ImageNet statistics). `f4 = fmap.mean(dim=(2,3))`; `layout4 = self.layout_squeeze(fmap).flatten(1)`; `logits4 = self.loc_logits(torch.cat([f4, layout4], dim=1))`; `logits = logits4.reshape(4, n, -1).mean(dim=0)`; `f = f4.reshape(4, n, -1).mean(dim=0)`. Everything from `p = torch.softmax(DECODE_BETA * logits, ...)` through the `conf = torch.sigmoid(z - self.conf_shift)` / `out = torch.cat(...)` / `return_logits` branch is BYTE-IDENTICAL to today, just with `self.conf_head` now taking `feat_ch=320` instead of `48`.
7) `loss_fn` is untouched (it already reads `GRID_K` as a module constant, so the 40x40 grid flows through automatically).
8) `export_onnx` is untouched -- it still produces the float32 ONNX; this becomes an intermediate artifact (see train.py step 4 below) rather than the final scored one.

model/train.py:
1) In `train_area`, replace the two-group optimizer with one group: `opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)` (delete `trunk_params`/`trunk_ids`/`head_params` entirely -- there is no pretrained/head LR distinction left to make).
2) Update `info["init"]` to `"from-scratch depthwise-separable trunk, weight-only 8-bit fake-quantization during training (straight-through), int8 dynamic quantization at export"` (replacing the old `"pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small ..."` string).
3) Leave `compute_cell_weights`, `prepare_realizations`, `sample_epoch`, `calibrate_conf_shift`, `CONFUSABILITY_ALPHA`, `TRAIN_REALIZATIONS`, `EPOCH_MULT`, and the epoch loop's structure completely untouched -- they already pick up the new `GRID_K` via the existing `from model.model import GRID_K, ...` import, no edits needed there.
4) After `export_onnx(model.cpu(), str(onnx_path))`, add: `from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic, QuantType` (import at top of file with the other imports); then `quantize_dynamic(model_input=str(onnx_path), model_output=str(onnx_path), weight_type=QuantType.QInt8)` -- quantizing in place so `models/<area>.onnx` (the path pipeline/score.py reads) IS the int8-weight artifact. Wrap this call so a failure is loud, not silently swallowed (let it raise -- no bare except). Add `info["exported_bytes_after_quantize"] = onnx_path.stat().st_size` to the returned info dict so the SQLite row logs the real deployed size for sanity-checking against pipeline/score.py's 4 MiB gate (this is informational logging only -- score.py re-measures the file independently and is the actual gate).

SANITY CHECK BEFORE HANDING OFF: after implementing, mentally (or via a quick local smoke run if the harness allows it) confirm the exported `models/<area>.onnx` file size is comfortably under 4 MiB (target: under ~3 MiB to leave margin, since this brief's channel widths are a starting estimate, not a verified one) and that `python -m autoresearch.backbonecheck --candidate model/model.py model/train.py` prints nothing. If the estimated size is too close to the gate, scale down block3's 320 channels (e.g. to 256) and/or GRID_K back toward 36 rather than touching anything else -- capacity headroom, not grid fineness, is this experiment's actual hypothesis.
